120	It was a very lucrative business in Europe, this matter of
121	loans with interest.
122	You get rich. Today there's also the business
123	of the heter iska, and I'll get to that shortly,
124	the heter iska and "making the sheretz tamei"; but first I'll
125	discuss the sugya, "either he's a drunkard," so either
126	he raises pigs, or he lends with interest, or he's a drunkard, because
127	his face was radiant. Rabbi Aba heard her
128	and said to her: "May a spirit blow in your face! If I have
129	any of these, may you die right here." Amen.
130	"If I have even one of those you mentioned. Rather, because
131	my Torah is fresh with me, my face is radiant, as it says: 'A man's wisdom
132	lights up his face.'" So the man's face is radiant
133	thanks to his wisdom. You see from the basis of
134	this Gemara that lending with interest was a lucrative business.
135	They made a huge amount of money from it. So if that's the case and they
136	really made a lot of money from it, why is it really forbidden?
137	Why can't I rent out money like I rent out household items? And more
138	than that,
139	the Torah says that whoever lends with interest
140	is wicked, denies HaShem, raises a hand against the Torah of Moshe
141	Rabbeinu, and has no share in the World to Come. Over what? I gave
142	him 100, I received 120, over those 20 that you charged. It could be
143	20, 20 thousand, 20 million, it makes no difference:
144	the law of a perutah is the law of 100, the law of what you took. So writes
145	the Rambam, quoting the Sages: "Whoever writes
146	interest" — he writes, and testifies against himself, that he denied
147	HaShem, the God of Israel.
148	And likewise, whoever borrows and lends with interest, even privately
149	between themselves, both of them deny HaShem, the God of Israel.
150	They denied the Exodus from Egypt, denied the miracles, denied
151	the splitting of the Red Sea. Why? Because of what is said:
152	"Your money you shall not give him with interest. I am HaShem your God
153	who took you out of the land of Egypt." So writes
154	the Rambam. It turns out that one who does such a thing is a heretic. There is
155	a practical difference in halachah. So what if he's a heretic? Fine,
156	I'm a heretic, so what's the problem? The problem is: they don't
157	sit shivah for him, he's buried with the wicked outside
158	the fence, they lower him into a pit, they look for
159	the opportunity to push him in; we are not commanded to revive
160	him if he fell into a well. Let him stay there, that will be the place of
161	his burial. And the Sages even cursed him: all his possessions
162	will collapse, and he will have no profit from it at all.
163	In Bava Metzia, page 75b, the Gemara asks: who transgressed
164	the prohibition, the borrower or the lender? The Gemara says:
165	the borrower, the lender, the witnesses, the guarantor, the scribe, everyone
166	involved in the deal,
167	all of them transgressed a prohibition.
168	You understand how severe this
169	matter is? All are partners, they transgress "before the blind,"
170	"do not place a stumbling block." And more than that, he does not rise
171	at the revival of the dead. Bava Metzia 61b: why did
172	the Merciful One write the Exodus from Egypt regarding interest? He mentions it to us
173	now in our parashah, the Exodus: "Do not charge interest," and so on, "I am
174	HaShem your God who took you out of the land of Egypt." Why
175	bring the Exodus into it together with interest? What
176	does interest have to do with the Exodus? The Holy One, blessed be
177	He, said, this is the Gemara in Bava Metzia 61: "I am the One who distinguished
178	between a drop of a firstborn and a drop that is not a firstborn's. I
179	will exact punishment from one who lends to Israel
180	with interest." Meaning, I will also
181	exact from one who lends without interest?
182	No: I will give him reward for that, because he did a mitzvah,
183	and I will exact punishment from one who lends with interest. So the Holy One,
184	blessed be He, says. Now, the punishment: he does not rise at the revival of the
185	dead, because then the Holy One, blessed be He, will distinguish between him
186	and one who is worthy of rising. And this punishment is brought
187	in Pirkei deRabi Eliezer 33, in the Gemara, and brought in Tosafot
188	in Bava Metzia, page 61b, and Sotah, page 4a. There it describes
189	the dead whom the prophet Yechezkel revived in the Valley of Dura.
190	There was a valley in the land of Babylon, and there were
191	dry bones — the well-known vision of the dry bones of
192	Yechezkel the prophet, one of the early prophets. And there
193	it describes how they all stood on their feet except one man
194	who did not stand on his feet. The Holy One, blessed be He, says
195	to him: Yechezkel, what do you see? He said to Him: a valley of bones.
196	He says to him: these bones are the House of Israel. Behold,
197	they say: "Our bones are dried up, we are cut off." Therefore
198	say to them: "Behold, I am opening your graves, My people, and I will bring you up
199	out of your graves, and I will put My spirit in you, and you shall live." Immediately
200	they stood up, an exceedingly great army. These were all those of the tribe of Ephraim
201	who had counted themselves before the Exodus from Egypt,
202	and miscalculated the end; in the end they all died there. And it is written that
203	all of them were revived, and one remained in his grave, did not rise. Yechezkel
204	the prophet asked the Holy One, blessed be He: Master
205	of the worlds, what is the matter with this one? The Holy One, blessed be
206	He, said to him: he lent with interest. So let him stay there below. He doesn't
207	believe that I provide a livelihood. What was the need for
208	this work, that you take, bring 100 and take
209	200? I'm not even talking about black-market loans,
210	you take 100 and return 1000. And if it's the gray market,
211	very nice. I wish you, my friends, knew
212	how to correct me: that's right, the gray market.
213	So this is extremely severe. This money has no
214	blessing, he does not rise at the revival of the dead, they don't sit shivah
215	for him. See how many severe things there are. Our teacher the Ari,
216	of blessed memory, explains the secret in the book Etz Chaim,
217	Shaar 18, page 85. He says that what remains on the grave, on the body
218	of a person, is the avelah.
219	In the language of the Kabbalists it is called "avelah digarma." There is
220	nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah. Beneath the nefesh there is something
221	smaller that remains when he goes to sleep. This
222	is called "kistah dechayuta." So he has a little
223	kistah dechayuta, but he has not died, Heaven forbid; he
224	is sleeping. When he dies, something remains that is even less than the kistah
225	dechayuta, which is called "avelah digarma," the avelah of the bones.
226	"Garma" means bones: the avelah of the bones. It is by this that we
227	come to the graves of tzaddikim and pray, because the soul
228	of the tzaddik, that is, his avelah digarma, remains there.
229	So we come to him, and therefore this soul is not
230	dry bones. They are bones soiled with sin,
231	from the root
232	"lach" (moist). They are not dry; they are bones that have in them
233	moisture,
234	through this moisture, the spiritual moisture that is found
235	on the bones. We come to the graves of tzaddikim; soon, before Rosh Hashanah, we do
236	a ziyarah at the graves of tzaddikim.
237	But the dead person is in Gan Eden. Why do you come
238	to pray by him? Rather, there is an avelah digarma on the grave,
239	and it is that, in whose merit he awakens at the revival
